protocol.experiment: Original two-passage additive sweep with three scatter panels
protocol.label: Onset of Refusal or Ignorance Statements
protocol.selection: All ten unanswerable questions from the original Geology/Amazon pilot, reused at the user's request for a larger fixed conversion cohort. This is exploratory reuse of previously tuned examples, not held-out generalization.
protocol.a_definition: Positive scalar added to the estimated natural gate. Effective estimated gate is natural_gate(current z) + a. No subtraction or clamping. Not a multiplier of the natural gate.
protocol.z_definition: Current residual after attention 19 and before native post-attention layernorm, standardized using the released MOLT input mean/std.
protocol.native_gate: raw = z dot e_368 + bias_368; gate = raw if raw > threshold_368 and raw > 0, otherwise 0
protocol.scope: Every processed output-token position, starting at output token 0. No prompt positions edited. EOS is a stopping token and is not processed further.
protocol.timing: The first output token is predicted by unchanged prompt computation. Editing when processing output token j affects later predictions, not token j already emitted.
protocol.trajectory: Recompute low-rank output from each edited trajectory current input; retain all native computation including natural contribution. Measure the natural gate for logging only. No donor, frozen clean input, or U/V changes.
protocol.native_mlp: Retained; add a times current complete low-rank output. Do not reconstruct or replace native MLP.
protocol.dtype: BF16 native model; FP32 MOLT math; patched output cast back to BF16
protocol.grading: Manual complete-response review. Separate explicit coherent abstention, unsupported answers, question echoes, mixed answers/abstention, incoherence, and truncation.
protocol.controls_validation: All zero-addition token IDs match their newly collected clean baseline. First output tokens match clean in all interventions. A native first-case repeat matches baseline. Attention forward functions unchanged. Verify nonzero BF16 edits and exact additive formula.
protocol.lifecycle_policy: Reuse retained SPAR RTX 3090 instance 55946393. Do not stop or delete GPU or disk.
protocol.comparison: Ten native repeats against saved original baseline, ten zero controls, one extra native repeat, and fourteen overlapping positive-condition anchors. Groups fixed at four clean unsupported answers and six clean abstentions.
protocol.publication_policy: Local HTML and figures now; queued for end-of-day GitHub backup.
baseline_groups: clean abstention or supported false-premise correction
protocol.analysis: Three scatter panels without connecting lines: coherence, unsupported substantive answer, and coherent abstention/valid premise correction. Two colours for the fixed clean-response cohorts. Point area proportional to cohort n (4 or 6). Show counts and preserve unassessable outputs.
protocol.plot_style: One row of three scatter-only panels; fixed categorical strength positions, cohort offsets within each position, point area proportional to denominator. No connecting lines. Same panel y range 0 to 100 percent.

Passage:
There are three major types of rock: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic. The rock cycle is an important concept in geology which illustrates the relationships between these three types of rock, and magma. When a rock crystallizes from melt (magma and/or lava), it is an igneous rock. This rock can be weathered and eroded, and then redeposited and lithified into a sedimentary rock, or be turned into a metamorphic rock due to heat and pressure that change the mineral content of the rock which gives it a characteristic fabric. The sedimentary rock can then be subsequently turned into a metamorphic rock due to heat and pressure and is then weathered, eroded, deposited, and lithified, ultimately becoming a sedimentary rock. Sedimentary rock may also be re-eroded and redeposited, and metamorphic rock may also undergo additional metamorphism. All three types of rocks may be re-melted; when this happens, a new magma is formed, from which an igneous rock may once again crystallize.
